name: Learn to Log Your Food
title: Diet changes - Beginner
description: Log at least one meal per day.

name: Reduce One Meat Meal
title: Diet changes - Beginner
description: Eat one fewer meat meal than during your previous week, while keeping in mind that eating less red meat is one of the most effective ways to reduce the environmental impact of your diet.

name: First Sustainable Swap
title: Diet changes - Beginner
description: Log 2 protein swap actions, while keeping in mind that replacing part of your meat intake with legumes can reduce the climate impact of your diet.

name: Discover Lentils
title: Diet changes - Beginner
description: Explore content and identify two nutritional or environmental benefits of lentils, while keeping in mind that quinoa contains all nine essential amino acids, making it a complete plant protein.

name: Two meat free days
title: Diet changes - Intermediate
description: Complete two meat-free days, while keeping in mind that producing beef requires much more land than producing plant proteins such as peas or tofu.

name: Sustainable Swap Builder
title: Diet changes - Intermediate
description: Log 4 protein swap actions, while keeping in mind that beans, lentils, peas and chickpeas are among the most sustainable protein sources available.

name: Legume Routine
title: Diet changes - Intermediate
description: Include legumes in four meals, while keeping in mind that millets are highly resilient crops that can grow in hot, dry conditions with little water.

name: Stay in the Green Zone
title: Diet changes - Advanced
description: Remain below four meat meals per week, while keeping in mind that livestock production uses most agricultural land globally while supplying a much smaller share of calories and protein.

name: Plant Protein Majority
title: Diet changes - Advanced
description: Obtain most protein-containing meals from non-meat protein sources, while keeping in mind that pulses naturally improve soil fertility by fixing nitrogen from the air, reducing the need for fertilizer.

name: Alternative Staples Habit
title: Diet changes - Advanced
description: Include alternative staple foods in at least five meals, while keeping in mind that quinoa is now cultivated in more than 70 countries, helping diversify global food production.

name: Origin Tracker
title: Product choices - Beginner
description: Look for the country of origin for at least 5 food products consumed during the week, while keeping in mind that about half of the world's habitable land is used for agriculture.

name: Water Behind Your Food
title: Product choices - Beginner
description: Around 70% of global freshwater withdrawals are used for agriculture. Then test what you have learned.

name: Climate Cost of Meals
title: Product choices - Beginner
description: Food systems generate about one-third of global greenhouse gas emissions. Then test what you have learned.

name: Food Miles Explained
title: Product choices - Beginner
description: Global food transport generates about 3 billion tonnes of CO₂-equivalent emissions each year. Then test what you have learned.

name: Product choices - Beginner
title: Product choices - Beginner
description: Make practical sustainable food choices in daily life.

name: Diverse Origins
title: Product choices - Intermediate
description: Track the origins of foods consumed and log at least 3 meals with locally produced products, while keeping in mind that beef is one of the most land-intensive foods people consume.

name: Wasted Food, Wasted Water
title: Product choices - Intermediate
description: Food waste also wastes enormous amounts of water used to grow food. Then test what you have learned.

name: Carbon Footprint of Meat
title: Product choices - Intermediate
description: Meat, especially beef and lamb, has a much higher carbon footprint than most plant foods. Then test what you have learned.

name: Transport Emissions Explorer
title: Product choices - Intermediate
description: Nearly one-fifth of the greenhouse gas emissions from the global food system come from transporting food. Then test what you have learned.

name: Product choices - Intermediate
title: Product choices - Intermediate
description: Make practical sustainable food choices in daily life.

name: Beyond Country of Origin
title: Product choices - Advanced
description: When selecting products for at least 3 meals, consider both country of origin and one additional sustainability indicator (e.g., certification, production method, seasonality), while keeping in mind that most agricultural land is used for livestock grazing or growing animal feed.

name: Water Footprint Deep Dive
title: Product choices - Advanced
description: The water footprint of your diet depends heavily on what you eat. Then test what you have learned.

name: Emissions Beyond the Plate
title: Product choices - Advanced
description: Food waste generates billions of tonnes of CO2-equivalent emissions annually. Then test what you have learned.

name: Cold Chain and Freight
title: Product choices - Advanced
description: Although food accounts for only about 18% of global freight transport distances, it produces around 27% of freight-related emissions. Then test what you have learned.

name: Product choices - Advanced
title: Product choices - Advanced
description: Make practical sustainable food choices in daily life.

name: NOVA Explorer
title: Production methods - Beginner
description: Look for the NOVA classification of at least 3 food products, while keeping in mind that food processing can improve food safety and extend shelf life.

name: Local Food, Closer Look
title: Production methods - Beginner
description: Short supply chains can support local economies and resilience. Then test what you have learned.

name: Production Method Observer
title: Production methods - Beginner
description: Look for information about how at least five food products were produced whenever this information is available, while keeping in mind that organic farms support higher biodiversity than conventional farms.

name: One Food, Many Steps
title: Production methods - Beginner
description: Pick one food product and explore of what may have happened between the raw ingredients and the final product you purchased, while keeping in mind that diversifying crops and breeds can increase food-system resilience.

name: Fair Trade Basics
title: Production methods - Beginner
description: Agriculture accounts for most child labour cases worldwide. Then test what you have learned.

name: Compare Processing Levels
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: Compare foods with different NOVA classifications on at least three products belonging to the same food category (e.g. three types of cheese), while keeping in mind that different processing methods use very different amounts of energy.

name: What Origin Labels Tell You
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: Food origin can provide useful information about traceability and sustainability. Then test what you have learned.

name: Production-Informed Choice
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: Use NOVA classification, Green-Score or ingredient-list information to guide at least five purchasing decisions. Use packaging, Open Food Facts or food-scanning applications, while keeping in mind that flower strips and pollinator habitats can support biodiversity on farms.

name: Breeding for Lower Impact
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: Breeding animals for lower methane emissions can reduce livestock impacts. Then test what you have learned.

name: The Social Side of Food
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: Food-system sustainability includes social and labour conditions. Then test what you have learned.

name: Multiple Indicators Tracker
title: Production methods - Intermediate
description: For four purchased foods, compare NOVA classification with either Green-Score or Nutri-Score.

name: Multi-Criteria Decisions
title: Production methods - Advanced
description: For at least three purchases, consider both NOVA classification and Green-Score before making a decision, while keeping in mind that not all processed foods have high environmental impacts.

name: Distance Is Not Everything
title: Production methods - Advanced
description: Local food is not always the most sustainable option. Then test what you have learned.

name: Farming Methods That Help
title: Production methods - Advanced
description: Agroforestry combines trees with crops or livestock on the same land. Then test what you have learned.

name: Innovation on the Farm
title: Production methods - Advanced
description: Genome editing may help develop crops that are more resilient to climate stress. Then test what you have learned.

name: Who Grows Our Food
title: Production methods - Advanced
description: Women play a critical role in food production but often have less access to resources. Then test what you have learned.

name: Packaging Material Observer
title: Packaging - Beginner
description: Identify the packaging material of at least five food products consumed during the week, while keeping in mind that food packaging protects products from contamination, moisture, oxygen and physical damage, helping maintain food safety and quality.

name: Reusable Packaging Spotter
title: Packaging - Beginner
description: Identify reusable or refillable food packaging options on at least five occasions, while keeping in mind that reusable packaging only becomes environmentally beneficial after it has been reused enough times.

name: Packaging-Informed Choices
title: Packaging - Intermediate
description: Consider packaging characteristics when making at least three purchasing decisions, while keeping in mind that the environmental impact of producing food is often much greater than the impact of the packaging used to protect it.

name: Reuse Opportunity Finder
title: Packaging - Intermediate
description: Choose reusable or refillable packaging options on at least two occasions this week, while keeping in mind that reusable packaging can reduce demand for virgin raw materials.

name: Multi-Criteria Packaging Decisions
title: Packaging - Advanced
description: For at least three purchases, consider both packaging material and end-of-life options before making a choice, while keeping in mind that edible packaging can help reduce reliance on fossil-based plastics by replacing conventional packaging materials with biodegradable alternatives.

name: Reuse Habit Builder
title: Packaging - Advanced
description: Use reusable or refillable packaging systems on at least five occasions. Look for products sold through deposit-return or refill systems, while keeping in mind that every reusable package has a break-even point where it becomes better than single-use alternatives.

name: Smart Serving Starter
title: Food waste - Beginner
description: Log 5 Half Plate Saved actions, while keeping in mind that households generate more food waste than any other sector in the European Union.

name: Storage Smarter
title: Food waste - Beginner
description: Make sure you read carefully packaging instructions on how to storage food after opening package for at least five products purchased, while keeping in mind that households account for more than half of food waste generated in the EU.

name: Date Label Explorer
title: Food waste - Beginner
description: Log 1 Expired Product Consumed action, while keeping in mind that more than half of all food waste in Europe is generated by households.

name: Portion Prediction Test
title: Food waste - Beginner
description: Before a meal, estimate how much food you think you will eat. After the meal, compare your estimate with what you actually consumed, while keeping in mind that portion sizes in many countries have increased substantially over recent decades.

name: Mission 3: Fridge Check Routine
title: Food waste - Intermediate
description: Perform a fridge or pantry check before a main shopping trip. Log at least 3 Expired Product Consumed actions or 3 Full Plate Saved actions, while keeping in mind that offering smaller portion sizes can reduce plate waste in canteens and restaurants.

name: Meal Planning Habit
title: Food waste - Intermediate
description: Create a meal plan before one main shopping trip, while keeping in mind that best-before dates refer to quality.

name: Mission 3: Fridge Check Routine
title: Food waste - Intermediate
description: Perform a fridge or pantry check before a main shopping trip. Log at least 3 Expired Product Consumed actions or 3 Full Plate Saved actions, while keeping in mind that household food waste in Europe is estimated at around 69 million tonnes per year.

name: Portion Control Pro
title: Food waste - Intermediate
description: Log at least Half Plate Saved actions, while keeping in mind that the environmental impact of a diet depends not only on what people eat but also on how much they eat.

name: Zero Plate Waste Focus
title: Food waste - Advanced
description: Log at least 7 Half Plate Saved actions, while keeping in mind that wasted meat contributes disproportionately to the climate impact of food waste.

name: Expiry Prevention Expert
title: Food waste - Advanced
description: Log 4 Expired Product Consumed actions, while keeping in mind that meat and dairy may be wasted less often but have a larger environmental footprint when wasted.

name: First-In, First-Out Expert
title: Food waste - Advanced
description: Throughout the week, organize your fridge, freezer or pantry so that foods with the shortest remaining shelf life are always placed at the front and used first, while keeping in mind that multi-buy offers and bulk discounts can encourage consumers to purchase more food than they can use.

name: Zero-Waste Planning Week
title: Food waste - Advanced
description: Plan all main meals for the week before your first shopping trip and only purchase foods that have a planned use, while keeping in mind that eating more food than the body needs increases demand for agricultural resources such as land, water and energy.

name: Protein Every Day
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Include a protein-rich food in at least one meal every day, while keeping in mind that protein helps build and repair muscles, tissues, enzymes and hormones.

name: Smart Snack Swap
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Log 5 Snack → Fruit or Nuts swaps, while keeping in mind that unsaturated fats are generally healthier than saturated fats.

name: Drink Upgrade
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Log 3 Sugary Drink → Water swaps, while keeping in mind that sugary drinks are a major source of added sugar in many diets.

name: Salt Spotter
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Choose one packaged food and determine how much salt it contains per 100 grams, while keeping in mind that most people consume more than twice the recommended salt intake.

name: Whole Grain Week
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Choose a whole-grain product every day. Select foods such as whole-grain bread, whole-wheat pasta, oats, brown rice, rye bread, quinoa or other whole grains, while keeping in mind that most Europeans consume less fibre than recommended.

name: Add One More Fruit or Vegetable
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: Add one extra serving of fruit or vegetables to your diet each day, while keeping in mind that vitamin D deficiency is common across Europe.

name: Calories Are Not Everything
title: Nutrition values - Beginner
description: The world already produces enough calories to feed everyone. Then test what you have learned.

name: Processed Meat Replacement
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Log 2 Processed Meat → Legumes swaps, while keeping in mind that most adults need about 0.83 g of protein per kilogram of body weight each day.

name: Healthy Fat Upgrade
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Choose a source of unsaturated fat instead of a source of saturated fat on at least five occasions, while keeping in mind that the type of fat you eat matters as much as the amount.

name: Drink Comparison
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Compare two sweet beverages that you enjoy drinking and identify which contains less sugar per 100 ml, while keeping in mind that WHO recommends limiting free sugars to less than 10% of daily energy intake.

name: Salt-Free Table
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Do not add salt to food at the table throughout the week, while keeping in mind that WHO recommends consuming less than 5 grams of salt per day.

name: Fibre With Every Meal
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Include at least one fibre-rich food in every main meal, while keeping in mind that adults should aim for at least 25 grams of fibre per day.

name: Vitamins From Your Plate
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Eating a diverse diet helps reduce the risk of vitamin deficiencies. Then test what you have learned.

name: Same Calories, Different Impact
title: Nutrition values - Intermediate
description: Foods providing the same number of calories can have very different environmental impacts. Then test what you have learned.

name: Complete Plant Proteins
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Eating a variety of plant proteins can provide all essential amino acids. Then test what you have learned.

name: Understanding Dietary Fats
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Fat should contribute no more than about 30% of total daily energy intake. Then test what you have learned.

name: Added Sugar Awareness Week
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Avoid foods or drinks with added sugars as one of the first three ingredients throughout the week, while keeping in mind that cooking at home makes it easier to control added sugar.

name: Sodium Hotspot
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Identify the food in your kitchen with the highest salt content per 100 grams, while keeping in mind that bread, processed meat and cheese are major sodium sources in Europe.

name: High-Fibre Breakfast Week
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Start every day with a breakfast containing a meaningful source of fibre. Build breakfast around oats, whole grains, fruit, seeds, nuts or other fibre-rich foods, while keeping in mind that higher fibre intake is linked to lower risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes.

name: Rainbow Week
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Consume foods from at least five different fruit and vegetable colours every day, while keeping in mind that vitamin B12 is found mainly in animal-based foods.

name: Nutrient-Dense Plate Week
title: Nutrition values - Advanced
description: Ensure that every main meal includes at least three of the following: a protein source, a fibre-rich food, a fruit or vegetable, or a source of healthy fats, while keeping in mind that feeding crops to livestock results in major calorie losses.
